ABIDE I: two analysts, one knowledge graph

An executed, illustrative experiment. Two hypothetical analysts work on the same public dataset (ABIDE I Preprocessed, C-PAC filt_noglobal, CC200 atlas). Analyst A asks a group-difference question in the style of Di Martino et al. 2014; Analyst B asks a prediction question in the style of Abraham et al. 2017. Every number below comes from results/*.json. Neither paper was replicated.

1. Cohorts are queries, not facts

Analyst A's cohort (441) is a strict subset of B's (767). Rater QC alone gives 873 participants; Abraham et al. report 871. The two-person difference is unresolved: the paper does not publish its list.

2. Analyst A: group difference

Edgewise model on 441 males from 9 sites: z_edge ~ ASD + age + FIQ + meanFD + site; OLS; BH-FDR q<0.05. 5428 of 19900 edges pass FDR; 5407 show lower connectivity in ASD (hypo fraction 0.996, bootstrap 95% CI 0.902-0.998). Median |d| among significant edges is 0.295: small effects.

3. Analyst B: prediction at unseen sites

4. They review each other

A reviews B. Of B's 199 most heavily weighted edges, 90 are among A's significant edges (expected by chance 54.3; hypergeometric p = 3.9e-08); signs agree in 90/90. Verdict: overlap exceeds chance.

B reviews A. On the 326 participants in B's cohort that A never used, A's hypoconnectivity signature gives pooled d = -0.080 (95% CI -0.312 to 0.152); 8 of 14 sites point the same way. Verdict: not established in independent participants. The signature correlates r = 0.981 with whole-brain mean connectivity, so it mostly measures a global shift that global-signal regression would remove.

5. A changes a shared rule; the graph says what to recheck

A tightens the shared motion rule from mean FD < 0.2 mm to < 0.15 mm. Before recomputing anything, SPARQL over the graph finds 63 affected participants in B's cohort and 38 in A's, 17 of 20 folds with an affected test participant, all 20 with an affected training participant, and one of A's sites (MAX_MUN) falling below the per-site minimum. After recomputation, 0 of 9 result families changed materially (rule: material if the v2 point estimate falls outside the v1 95% interval (bootstrap for pooled AUC and A's hypo fraction), or a review verdict string changes).

6. Phenotype embedding, joined to imaging

UMAP of age, FIQ, VIQ and PIQ queried from the graph (604 complete cases, 163 dropped for missing values, 15 sites). Trustworthiness (k=15) 0.977 vs PCA 0.920; other seeds 0.973, 0.974; 15-neighbour overlap across seeds 0.868, 0.857. Silhouette by diagnosis 0.025, by site -0.337. Mean cortical thickness (ANTs) correlates with age at Spearman 0.026.

Adding SRS leaves 255 complete cases from 4 sites: the missingness pattern, not biology, decides who is embedded.

7. Validation

Local SHACL profile (17 shapes) over 296,763 triples: conforms = True. Mutation tests rejected: 8/8 (connectivity derivative without source; review without reviewer; claim typed as causal; evidence span not verbatim; fold with no test participants; activity snapshot without timestamp; promote a study-only record to the lake; promotion candidate missing a gate). Paper quotes matching the source text verbatim: 18/18. This checks structure and provenance, not scientific correctness.

9. Joining ReproNim's simple2 NIDM graphs

24 ABIDE site graphs and 3 tool CDE files from ReproNim/simple2_NIDM_examples (commit e0dff17629) were loaded unmodified as named graphs. Their own simple2_query.sparql, unmodified, returns 155,528 rows for 989 participants in 117.4 s with Oxigraph. It reproduces their shipped output for 12,907/12,907 participant x measure keys; the only differences are 3 ANTs measures whose labels changed since that CSV was written (CSF Volume (mm^3), GVol (mm^3), WVol (mm^3) -> CSFVOL (mm^3), GMVOL (mm^3), WMVOL (mm^3)). Identity join through the shared ndar:src_subject_id literal: 1112/1112 matched, 0 age/sex/diagnosis/FIQ conflicts.

Median Pearson r across 17 regions: ANTs vs FSL 0.53, ANTs vs FreeSurfer 0.82, FSL vs FreeSurfer 0.52. FSL's CSF is total CSF while FreeSurfer and ANTs report the ventricular label under the same UBERON term.

10. Conforming to the current NIDM schema

PyNIDM v4.5.5 ships a LinkML schema written for AI-assisted SPARQL generation. SHACL generated from it (open shapes): abide_core: 11,491 results on 292,437 triples; pynidm_csv2nidm_phenotype: 134 results on 105,641 triples; repronim_simple2_Caltech: 114 results on 22,747 triples. The same three schema slots account for nearly all results, including in PyNIDM's own output and ReproNim's files (association agents limited to persons, an export-activity shape that targets every prov:Activity, single-valued Derivative.used). Terms the schema has no slot for are declared in graph/abide_extension.ttl (13 classes, 191 properties).

What did not run

  • No raw MRI was downloaded or reprocessed; preprocessing is taken as released by ABIDE Preprocessed.
  • Neither paper was replicated: different pipeline versions, atlases, cohorts and models (see the comparability assessments in the graph).
  • The analysts, their reviews and the rule revision are a simulation; no real person's work is represented.
  • Abraham 2017 quotes are from the arXiv v1 preprint, not the journal version.
